The '''TIE/D automated fighter''', or '''droid/drone TIE fighter''', was a [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] used by the reborn [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] during his attacks on the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] in [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]].

==Characteristics==
The [[TIE/D]] [[Droid/Legends|automated]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] took the standard [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] command pod with [[Twin ion engine/Legends|twin ion engines]] and twin [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]], additional armor plating and rectangular wing panels with adjustable pitch were added. Despite their heavier armor, they could actually reach a higher atmospheric speed than the [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN interceptors]]&mdash;overall, they were fast, small, and very expendable. A single TIE/D cost 170,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].

The starfighter had rectangular solar arrays with a movable wing servo to fuel the power generator. The 6.3 [[Meter/Legends|meter]]-long craft was capable of 100 [[Megalight|MGLT]]. Instead of a living pilot, the craft was equipped with a [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]] [[Ace-6 droid brain]]. The 10-[[Kilogram/Legends|kilogram]] unit allowed [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]] to increase the TIE/D's shielding.<ref name="RS I">[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]</ref>

==History==
[[File:TIEdroid_egvv.jpg|thumb|left|180px|[[TIE series/Legends|TIE]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]].]]
The TIE/D was initially developed by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Arndall Lott]], one of many post-[[Battle of Endor/Legends|Endor]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]].<ref name="DE">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]''</ref> Sienar Fleet Systems engineers based the TIE/D on their original [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]], and as a result, many of the vehicle's design elements came from the standard TIE.<ref name="DB">[[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]]</ref>

With the automation experiment of the [[Katana fleet|''Katana'' fleet]] as his original inspiration, General Lott's first attempts at automated combat systems were based on [[Slave circuit|slaving]] multiple war machines to a single remote [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]]. Though this method saw limited success, its overall inefficiency and susceptibility to jamming prompted a new approach.<ref name="DE" />

The [[Droid starfighter/Legends|droid starfighters]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] provided Imperial scientists with the basis for a new automated fighter. Every TIE/D had an integrated Cybot Galactica Ace-6 droid brain which could be updated with new tactics&mdash;despite this, it was still often easily outwitted by sentient starfighter pilots.<ref name="DB" />

<div style="float:right">[[File:TieDSquad.jpg|thumb|180px|TIE/D automated starfighters swarm out from inside a World Devastator.]]</div>

The finalized version of the TIE/D debuted against the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] on [[Dac/Legends|Dac]], six years after the Battle of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]. The Imperial [[World Devastator]]s invaded the world in the [[Battle of Calamari]], and their internal factories made swarms of TIE/Ds from the elements of the very world they attacked.<ref name="DE" />

During the battle, TIE/D fighters were pitted against New Republic [[V-wing airspeeder|V-wings]] and [[E-7 E-wing multi-role starfighter|E-wings]].<ref name="DE" /> The massive numbers of TIE/Ds provided them with an inherent advantage, but New Republic pilots were able to outwit these drones just as [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Clone trooper pilot/Legends|clone]] and [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] pilots were able to outwit [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] droid starfighters in the past.<ref name="DB" /> The New Republic's [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] battled and defeated squadrons of the automated starfighters, which were attacking [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[City/Legends|cities]].<ref name="RS I" /> At a similar time, squadrons of TIE/D starfighters also destroyed the [[Mandator III-class dreadnought|''Mandator III''-class dreadnought]] ''[[Aculeus]]''.

When the tide turned against the Empire on Mon Calamari, most of their TIE/D manufacturing capability was destroyed along with the World Devastators.<ref name="DB" />

Robotic TIE Fighters were found abandoned in [[Supreme Warlord]] [[Blitzer Harrsk|Harrsk's]] [[Deep 3]] Shipyard. However, it is unknown if they are the same model. These were subsequently used by the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] well into the Yuuzhan Vong War.

==Behind the scenes==
After premiering in the ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]'' comic book, the TIE/D was the first [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] set, released in the TIE Collection set (10131).
